quotes.text:
* MboxMsgOutputStream writes a single message out to an underlying mbox
 * stream.
 * It's a nsISafeOutputStream so callers need to "commit" the written data
 * by calling nsISafeOutputStream::Finish() when done.
 * Just calling Close(), or letting the stream go out of scope will
 * cause a rollback, and the underlying mbox file will be truncated back
 * to the size it was.

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: MboxMsgOutputStream is an nsISafeOutputStream. Finish commits the message; Close or destruction attempts rollback to the starting position. Current rollback flushes buffered data before Seek/SetEOF and keeps a rollback error when closing the inner stream also fails. Finish rolls back an earlier write error or final separator failure. Do not equate closing with successful commit. This is a current-source extension of the 374 ownership check; later Bug 1960252 is cited by the code but was not read externally. No storage-failure injection was run.
title: Commit an mbox message explicitly and preserve the rollback error
